title: Admin-only movie video attachment upload and in-app playback

requirements.summary: Allow admins to attach/upload a movie video file (bytes) and enable Movie Detail playback from stored video while keeping URL-based playback compatible.
acceptanceCriteria: The backend exposes admin-guarded methods to upload and retrieve a movie video file (bytes) associated with a movie
Non-admin callers cannot upload, replace, or delete stored movie video files
In the admin movie create/edit dialog, a file input is available for attaching a video file and is only shown/usable for admins
After uploading a video file for a movie, the movie detail page can play the uploaded video successfully
Existing URL-based video playback continues to work for movies that still use a video URL (backwards compatible)

file_operations.description: Align frontend Movie typing with current UI needs by ensuring the Movie type supports both URL-based playback (e.g., optional videoUrl) and the uploaded attachment (videoBlob: ExternalBlob), matching the canister interface used by the app.

Add an admin-only video file attachment input to the create/edit dialog using the existing authorization hook (authorization component) to hide/disable for non-admins; on submit, pass selected file data so the admin can upload it via blob-storage ExternalBlob. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Extend movie create/edit mutations to optionally upload/replace the attached video after successful metadata save by calling the existing uploadMovieVideo backend capability; use the blob-storage ExternalBlob wrapper (ExternalBlob.fromBytes and optional withUploadProgress) and invalidate relevant movie queries on success. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Update the video player to prefer playing the uploaded attachment when available by using blob-storage ExternalBlob.getDirectURL() for the video source, and fall back to the existing movie video URL field when no attachment exists (backwards compatible). Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
